title: Complex numbers: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Roots That Vanish | the constant term of y = x^2 - 4x + c dragged until the parabola lifts off the x-axis, with the discriminant, the quadratic formula and sqrt of a negative all computed live | the moment b^2 - 4ac goes negative the formula asks for sqrt(-1), so i is defined by i^2 = -1 and sqrt(-k) = i*sqrt(k), and the two roots arrive as a conjugate pair

2. The Powers Cycle | the exponent n slid from 0 to 24 against a four-stop wheel of 1, i, -1, -i, with the division n = 4q + r worked out beside it | i^1 through i^4 are derived from i^2 = -1 alone, i^4 = 1 makes the powers repeat with period 4 (not 2), so any power is answered by the remainder mod 4

3. Parts Stay Apart | four coefficient sliders and an add/subtract toggle feeding a two-column ledger and a tip-to-tail picture on the complex plane | adding and subtracting combines real with real and imaginary with imaginary and never mixes them, and the minus sign in a subtraction must reach both parts of the second number

4. Foil Then Fold | the four FOIL products of (a + bi)(c + di) laid out in a grid, with a toggle between folding i^2 to -1 and pretending it is +1 | multiplication is the binomial expansion plus one fold, the bd*i^2 term becomes real and lands in the real part with its sign flipped, giving (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i

5. Conjugate Clears i | a division worked step by step, with a switch between multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator and the conjugate of the numerator | the conjugate of a + bi is a - bi and (a + bi)(a - bi) = a^2 + b^2 is always real, which is why only the denominator's conjugate turns a fraction into standard form
